problem: End-to-end VLN agents in continuous environments (VLN-CE) mostly encode raw RGB-D frames with LSTM memory. They lack structured, semantically meaningful spatial memory and spatio-temporal reasoning, and they generalize poorly to unseen scenes on long-horizon (~55 low-level steps) episodes. Simply feeding a semantic map to existing VLN-CE models (Seq2Seq, CMA) does not help consistently.
motivation: VLN-CE removes the nav-graph assumption and requires long action sequences, so the agent must track which parts of the instruction it has completed and relate language cues to the surrounding layout. Structured memories (occupancy or semantic maps) have helped visual navigation, but they had not been effectively combined with language for VLN-CE. The authors observe that naive map inclusion can even hurt, which motivates an explicit cross-modal alignment between the map and the instruction.
key_idea: Build an egocentric top-down semantic map at every step and align it with the instruction through transformer self- and cross-attention (SLAM-T). Fuse this with RGBD-language cross-attention features, then decode actions with a hybrid RNN + cross-modal transformer decoder that reasons over both time and the instruction.
insight: The gain comes from how semantics are grounded in language, not from having semantics at all. Baselines that receive the semantic map as extra input (Seq2Seq-SM, CMA-SM) do not reliably improve and sometimes degrade: Seq2Seq-SM teacher-forcing val-unseen SPL is 0.15 vs 0.16 for Seq2Seq, and DAgger val-seen SPL is 0.28 vs 0.31. In SASRA's val-seen ablation, adding SLAM-T gives +4 SR / +3 SPL (row 2→3), replacing the plain RNN decoder with the Hybrid Action Decoder gives +5 SR / +5 SPL (row 1→3), and DAgger on top gives +9 SR / +9 SPL (row 3→4), showing that exposure bias is a major factor in VLN-CE.
method: Local semantic map construction: depth pixels are back-projected to a point cloud with camera intrinsics and moved to the world frame using the agent pose. Points are projected to 2D as obstacle (height threshold) or free space, and obstacle cells store the semantic class from the semantic sensor. The result is an agent-centred 2r×2r multi-hot 'Bag of Semantic Indices' map (r=40, downscaled by 1/2 to r/2×r/2 for memory).

Language Encoder Transformer: word embeddings plus fixed sinusoidal positional encoding pass through stacked multi-head self-attention and feed-forward blocks to give the instruction encoding v (H=512, 4 heads, FF size 1024).

SLAM-T (Semantic-Linguistic Attention Map Transformer): a Gaussian-kernel 2D relative positional encoding (GPE) centred on the agent (scale r/2) is added to the map. Self-attention over map cells is followed by cross-attention in which map features are the queries and the instruction encoding v is the keys/values, yielding (r×r)×H cross-modal map features.

RGBD-Linguistic Cross-Attention Transformer: RGB uses an ImageNet ResNet-50 (7×7×2048), reduced by 1×1 conv and adaptive-pooled to 4×4. Depth uses a DD-PPO-pretrained ResNet-50 (4×4×128). The two are early-fused by channel concatenation, then passed through self-attention with a learned 2D positional encoding and cross-attention to v.
Late fusion: the SLAM-T features are average-pooled over space and concatenated with the RGBD-language features along the hidden dimension to form the visual-linguistic embedding V_t.

Hybrid Action Decoder: an RNN over [V_t, a_{t-1}] gives hidden state h_t. A cross-modal transformer then uses h_t (plus positional encoding) as query/key and the instruction v as value to track instruction progress. An MLP + softmax outputs the action over {forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 15°, stop}.

Training: cross-entropy imitation learning with inflection weighting 3.2, teacher forcing (≤20 epochs, early stopping on val-seen), then DAgger fine-tuning (3 rounds, β=0.75, 4 epochs per round). Adam with a cyclical learning rate, 3× RTX 2080 Ti, Habitat-API 0.1.5.

setting.backbone: ImageNet ResNet-50 (RGB) + DD-PPO-pretrained ResNet-50 (depth) + Transformer language/cross-modal encoders + RNN/Transformer hybrid action decoder (trained with imitation learning)
setting.training_data: VLN-CE (R2R converted to Habitat) train split: 10819 episodes from 61 MP3D scenes. Teacher forcing followed by DAgger aggregation (3 rounds). No extra or augmented instruction data.
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB + depth + simulator semantic segmentation + agent pose (used to build a local top-down semantic map)
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN LEFT/RIGHT 15° / STOP
setting.privileged: Ground-truth per-pixel semantic labels from the simulator's semantic sensor (and simulator depth), plus the agent pose used to register the semantic map ('We use the depth and semantic label of pixels from the simulation environment').

numbers_note: Metrics are printed as fractions (e.g., 0.24) and converted here to 0-100. Table II (ablation, val-seen only) row 4 (SM+HAD+DAgger) reports SR 0.36, SPL 0.34, nDTW 0.54, TL 9.19, NE 7.03. Its SR and SPL match Table I, but its nDTW, TL and NE differ from Table I's DAgger val-seen row (0.53 / 8.89 / 7.17); this is an internal inconsistency. The other ablation rows on val-seen are: w/o HAD (SM only, TF) SR 0.22 / SPL 0.20 / nDTW 0.41 / TL 11.07 / NE 9.09; w/o SM (HAD only, TF) SR 0.23 / SPL 0.22 / nDTW 0.42 / TL 8.30 / NE 8.78. There are no test-unseen (leaderboard) results. All baselines were retrained on the authors' Habitat build, so the numbers are not directly comparable to published VLN-CE numbers.
results: On VLN-CE val-unseen with DAgger, SASRA reaches SR 0.24 / SPL 0.22 / nDTW 0.47 / NE 8.32, versus the strongest retrained baseline CMA-DAgger at SR 0.20 / SPL 0.18. This is the claimed >22% relative SPL gain; the gain over Seq2Seq-DAgger (SPL 0.17) is +5 absolute. On val-seen, SASRA-DAgger reaches SR 0.36 / SPL 0.34 vs 0.32 / 0.31 for Seq2Seq-DAgger. Baselines given the same semantic map (Seq2Seq-SM, CMA-SM) are +5 to +6 SPL behind SASRA and do not consistently beat their map-free versions.
limitations: Relies on ground-truth semantic segmentation (and pose/depth) from the simulator to build the semantic map, so real-world performance with predicted semantics and noisy pose is untested.

Absolute performance is low (24% SR val-unseen). Comparisons are only against baselines the authors retrained on their own Habitat build, without the published VLN-CE enhancements such as progress monitoring or augmentation, and there is no test-set or leaderboard evaluation.
The ablation is run only on val-seen, and its full-model row does not exactly match the main table; no real-robot experiments.
